third_seed_stability_diagnostic.interpretation: The final point is within 1% of best, but the final qualifying suffix spans only 400 steps. Keep stable=null under the predefined rule.

conclusions: All three matched seeds improve best validation AbsRel from 200 to 400 images. Mean changes from 0.097696 to 0.095421 (about 2.33% relative reduction); paired difference -0.002275 with scene-bootstrap 95% interval [-0.004262, -0.000488]. This supports a validation-set gain under the fixed recipe; it is not a new official test result. Seed SD and conditional scene uncertainty are reported separately.

All three seeds lose boundary F1: mean 0.459486 to 0.450541, paired difference -0.008945 with interval [-0.011122, -0.006885]. Boundary-band AbsRel improves in all three, from 0.157997 to 0.155557; difference -0.002440 with interval [-0.004117, -0.000770]. Better depth values near boundaries do not imply sharper or better-localized discontinuities.

Best RMSE and delta1 improve as point estimates in all three seeds, but their scene intervals still cross zero. Final checkpoints also improve overall AbsRel, RMSE, delta1 and boundary-band AbsRel relative to matched R200, while losing boundary F1; the corresponding final paired intervals exclude zero. Best and final remain separate endpoints.

Relative to shared B0, R400 improves overall depth and boundary-band errors, with descriptive scene intervals excluding zero. Boundary F1 differs by -0.000613 and its interval [-0.003691, 0.002758] crosses zero, so this group does not establish a boundary-F1 improvement over the original model.

Terminal stability is 2/3, compared with 0/3 for R200. Seeds 320112 and 320113 qualify from steps 4300 and 4800. Seed 320114 has validation rebounds at 4000 and 4100; after recovering at 4200, only 400 qualifying steps remain before stopping at 4600. Its final error is within 1% of best, but that single endpoint does not meet the 500-step stability rule.

Best steps are 4900/5700/3700 and stop steps 5300/5900/4600, all by patience. Raw best and the significant-improvement anchor are different: third-seed patience runs from its step-3600 anchor, despite a small new raw best at 3700. Complete curves preserve plateaus, rebounds and the declining online training loss; no intermediate detailed boundary scores were measured.

The common 0.10 target is confirmed at 2700/2600/2400 updates, averaging 2567 versus 2200 for R200. No seed reaches 0.09. More images yield a lower observed optimum here, but not fewer updates to the fixed common target. Mean stopping iterations increase from 4100 to 5267, while effective epochs decrease because each epoch contains more images.

R400 costs 3479.36/4203.20/3016.57 seconds of recorded cumulative training and evaluation, with zero AMP skips and 768.706 MiB peak allocated GPU memory in each run. Mean time is 3566.38 seconds versus 1057.96 for R200. These are observations on the shared laptop, excluding historical shared feature preparation; the time ratio cannot be attributed solely to data count.

The four reviewed plots now show three R400 seeds. Their best errors are close, but third-seed stopping and stability differ. Other methods at 400 images and the planned 300-image level are not yet complete; connecting lines are not estimates for missing runs. The final adjacent-count analysis will use 200-to-300 and 300-to-400 after those runs exist.

Fixed first-seed observations remain mixed: cafe depth values improve, an interior-wall case regresses, and shelf edge matching worsens despite lower overall error. The first-seed review contains the actual image evidence. All 12 newly saved third-seed best/final arrays reproduce nine metrics/counts exactly; full validation CSV means and checkpoint identities are also verified.

Continue the unchanged queue through LoRA and Joint at 400 images and all later counts/stages. This review adds no architecture search, altered training schedule, full-795 refit, or new 654-image test evaluation.
